title: Quantization performance/quality tradeoffs: INT8/FP8/GPTQ/AWQ (kernels)
content:
Objective:

This doc captures a focused set of benchmarks and profiling notes to understand performance vs. quality tradeoffs for different quantization strategies (INT8, FP8, GPTQ, AWQ) and kernel implementations in the serving runtime. Goal is to produce guidance for:
- which quantization modes are recommended by workload (chat vs. generation vs. embeddings),
- kernel choices and micro-optimizations that matter at scale,
- expected latency/throughput/memory outcomes and quality regressions to watch for,
- actionable next steps for rollout (canary profiles, fallback policies).

Scope and constraints:
- Models: evaluation done on Llama-2-13B and MPT-7B as representative decoder-only workloads. Small checks on Llama-2-70B (reduced sequence lengths) for memory scaling.
- Hardware: NVIDIA A10G (AVX5) and H100 (SXM) clusters; tests run on dedicated GPU nodes to avoid noisy neighbors.
- Runtime: current main branch serving-runtime with latest kernel selector and batching enabled. All runs use the same tokenizer and identical seeds for deterministic eval where applicable.
- Datasets: 1) standard pass@1 generation set (2k prompts) for throughput/latency; 2) LM-eval style benchmark (PiQA, Lambada, StoryCloze) for quality/perplexity; 3) synthetic long-context prefix set for KV-cache stress tests.
- Metrics: 90th percentile latency (p90), median latency (p50), tokens/sec (throughput), GPU memory (peak), end-to-end latency (including network), and quality metrics (perplexity, accuracy/EM where applicable).

Quantization modes tested:
- FP32 baseline (reference)
- INT8 (static per-channel symmetric quantization where supported)
- FP8 (E4M3 profile with calibrated scaling)
- GPTQ (4-bit GPTQ variants used via offline quantizer)
- AWQ (approximate weight quantization - 4/8-bit modes)

Kernel variants and runtime flags:
- Default fused attention kernel (baseline)
- Optimized matmul kernel (blocked GEMM with pre-packed weights)
- KV cache-optimized kernels (reduced memory copy, direct mapped KV)
- Mixed-precision execution flag (mixed-fp16 where applicable)
- Per-layer dequantization on-the-fly vs. pre-dequantized weight cache

High-level findings (summary):
- INT8 gives the most consistent throughput uplift (1.6-2.1x tokens/sec) across Llama-2-13B and MPT-7B with minimal quality regressions on common reasoning benchmarks (<= 1.5% drop).
- FP8 can approach INT8 throughput on H100 with optimized kernels but is more sensitive to scale calibration; quality regressions are similar to INT8 for short-context generation but worsen on reasoning-heavy prompts.
- GPTQ (4-bit) yields the biggest memory savings and can reduce p90 latency in memory-bound scenarios by up to 30% vs FP32 but shows larger quality variance on Lambada/StoryCloze (3-7% delta).
- AWQ modes (4-bit hybrid) balance quality vs. memory; when using per-block re-scaling they maintain quality within ~2-3% of FP32 while giving 1.8-2.4x throughput depending on kernel packing.
- Kernel selection matters: pre-packed weight GEMM with on-GPU quantized representations reduces p50 latency by 12-18% relative to naive per-request dequantization approaches.
- KV-cache optimized kernels reduce end-to-end latency for long-context synthetic workloads by 20-40% for quantized models that avoid extra memory copies.

Representative benchmark tables (verbal):
- Llama-2-13B on A10G, batch=8, seq_len=512, temp=0.7:
  - FP32: p50=180ms, p90=320ms, tokens/sec=28, GPU_mem=25GB, perplexity=12.6
  - INT8: p50=95ms, p90=170ms, tokens/sec=52, GPU_mem=14GB, perplexity=12.8
  - FP8: p50=110ms, p90=200ms, tokens/sec=44, GPU_mem=13GB, perplexity=13.1
  - GPTQ-4bit: p50=125ms, p90=220ms, tokens/sec=38, GPU_mem=9.5GB, perplexity=13.9
  - AWQ-4bit-hybrid: p50=100ms, p90=185ms, tokens/sec=47, GPU_mem=11GB, perplexity=13.0

- Notes on variance: p90 is sensitive to kernel GC and memory spikes when using host-side dequantization. Runs where dequantization happened on CPU showed p90 inflation (up to +40ms) and larger variance.

Profiling notes (methodology):
- Use NVIDIA Nsight and CUPTI traces to capture kernel-level timings. Aggregate traces with perfetto for timeline views.
- Record per-request microevents: tokenize, encode, forward (per layer), kv-update, decode. Instrument runtime to emit timestamps for each stage.
- Important hotspots observed:
  1) per-request weight dequantization (CPU->GPU copies) when not using prepacked quantized weights; worst for GPTQ which required extra gather/unpack ops
  2) attention softmax kernel tail calls for long sequences (memory-bound)
  3) synchronization stalls due to blocking memory copies for KV cache writes
  4) small-batch GEMM efficiency (batching policy needed to keep GPU utilization)

Quality evaluation details:
- For perplexity and LM tasks, we used deterministic sampling (temp=0.0) where applicable to keep results comparable. For open-ended generation we used nucleus sampling with fixed RNG seeds and compared human-readable metrics (BLEU-ish proxies, prompt-completion overlap).
- Observed failure modes by quantization type:
  - INT8: occasional token-level shifts (subtle), mostly harmless for chat UX but can flip top-1 answers in tight QA tasks
  - FP8: calibration-sensitive; edge-case numeric instability on certain layers (layernorm), requires per-layer fine-tune or recalibration
  - GPTQ: some rare hallucination spikes on reasoning tasks; mitigation via targeted fine-tuning or layerwise FP16 fallback for critical layers
  - AWQ: generally stable, but block-size choices affect local representation quality (tuning needed)

Recommendations for rollout and runtime defaults:
- Default offering: INT8 with pre-packed weight cache + optimized matmul kernel. Int8 gives best balance of throughput and low/no quality regressions for most customers.
- Premium profile: AWQ-4bit hybrid for customers needing extra memory reduction but still wanting decent quality. Recommend canary on production traffic with replayed prompt set.
- Experimental: GPTQ-4bit and FP8 for cost-sensitive workloads; require stricter QA and opt-in customer flags. Provide automatic fallback to INT8/FP32 on quality regressions.
- Runtime flags to expose: quant_mode (fp32|int8|fp8|gptq|awq), kernel_pack (auto|prepacked|dequant_on_fly), kv_mode (direct|copy), batch_hint (small|medium|large).

Action items / next steps:
- [ ] Run full sweep on Llama-2-70B (reduced seq length) on H100 to validate memory scaling for AWQ/GPTQ (owner: Daniel Kim, due: 2025-12-10)
- [ ] Add per-layer calibration step to FP8 pipeline and re-run FP8 calibrations on reasoning benchmarks (owner: Lina Rodriguez, due: 2025-12-08)
- [ ] Implement a canary config that uses AWQ on 1% of production requests for customers on Dedicated; add automatic rollback on quality regressions exceeding 2% (owner: Marcus Chen, due: 2025-12-15)
- [ ] Add trace correlation to console dashboards: surface p90 delta when quant_mode changes and expose top-k regression prompts (owner: Eng Observability, ticket JIRA-RT-2200)

Open questions / risks:
- How to automate per-customer quantization selection based on historical latency/quality SLAs? (R&D item)
- Need to validate legal/compliance implications of quantized artifacts storage (some customers consider model weights CII).
- Long-tail correctness regressions (rare hallucination cases) — propose periodic re-evals and human-in-the-loop review for high-risk customers.

Appendix (short runbook notes):
- To reproduce local benchmark: checkout branch perf/quant-bench, run tools/bench/run_bench.sh --model llama-2-13b --quant int8 --kernel prepacked --batch 8 --seq 512 --trace nsight.out
- To collect traces: set env TRACE_BACKEND=perfetto; run bench with --collect-trace; convert with tools/trace/convert_perfetto.py
- Helpful tickets/PRs: see linked_artifacts above.

Draft notes (working):
- We should capture a short benchmark CSV per model/config in the artifacts bucket and reference them from the Confluence perf page.
- Consider an automated nightly job that runs the short sweep (FP32, INT8, AWQ) on a small subset of prompts and surfaces percent delta in Console as a regression flag.

Sign-off: Aisha Patel (eng-serving-runtime).
